elements.quote: A living systematic review of the literature was designed, consulting the electronic online versions of the CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline PyscoDoc, PsycoINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in November 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly labels the study as 'A living systematic review'.

elements.quote: The objective of this study is to identify the best available scientific evidence on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs in terms of stress, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy.
elements.reason: The abstract states a clear main objective/review question.

elements.quote: Original research was selected, published in either English, Spanish, French, Italian, or Portuguese.
elements.reason: The abstract reports at least some inclusion criteria (study type and permitted languages) but does not specify the full set of main inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., population specifics, date limits, outcomes) in the abstract.

elements.quote: consulting the electronic online versions of the CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline PyscoDoc, PsycoINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in November 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched and specifies the date (November 2021) when searches were performed.
The abstract does not describe the methods used to assess risk of bias; although methods are described elsewhere in the manuscript, this information is not present in the abstract text.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to present or synthesize results (e.g., narrative synthesis, meta-analysis) within the abstract text.

elements.quote: In total, 2082 publications were identified, of which 16 were included in this review.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (16) and the number of records identified, but does not report the total number of participants or summarize key study characteristics in the abstract.

elements.quote: The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected. Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety; in the case of depressive symptoms, it was having a clinical history of illnesses that could weaken their defenses against infection. Stopping unpleasant emotions and thoughts was the coping strategy most frequently used by these HPs.
elements.reason: The abstract presents main outcome results and associated factors but does not provide the number of studies or participants contributing to each outcome or quantitative estimates in the abstract.

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity between the participants, in the area of development, in the scales and measurement instruments used, and with the final results.
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was not conducted for this review, so reporting a summary estimate and interval in the abstract is not applicable.

elements.quote: Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety;
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect for a comparison (women had greater risk than men) and specifies which group is at greater risk.
The abstract does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision) in the abstract text.

elements.quote: The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected. Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety; ... Stopping unpleasant emotions and thoughts was the coping strategy most frequently used by these HPs.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a concise interpretation of the results and their implications regarding factors associated with worse mental health and common coping strategies.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name or registration number; although registration is reported elsewhere in the manuscript, it is not included in the abstract text.

elements.quote: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?'
elements.reason: The review states an explicit objective framed as a research question using a question-formulation framework (PIO), specifying population (HPs providing out-of-hospital care), exposure (possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2), and outcomes (mental health).

elements.quote: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?'
elements.reason: The review addresses effects of exposure on mental health (observational/exposure question) and is not a review of intervention effects; therefore specifying planned comparisons using PICO for interventions does not apply.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) being original, (2) based on qualitative and/or quantitative methods, (3) with any methodological design, (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, (7) without geographic limitation, (8) with at least the abstract available, and (9) that in their results evaluated the impact of possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 on levels of stress, anxiety, depression and/or self-efficacy of the HPs who were working in public, private, or voluntary out-of-hospital EMS during the COVID-19 pandemic or identified factors related positively or negatively with these levels or compared them with those obtained in other working environments and/or professional categories.
elements.reason: The methods section lists explicit study characteristics used to determine eligibility: study designs, qualitative/quantitative methods, submission/peer-review status, languages, date cutoff, geographic scope, abstract availability, settings (out-of-hospital EMS), and outcomes of interest.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: ... (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, ...
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria explicitly specify report characteristics including publication/language requirements and a date restriction (completed after December 2019) and peer-review/publication status.

elements.quote: Opinion articles and editorials, studies of low scientific-technical quality, those that did not reply to the posed research question and/or were not in line with the objective of the review, as well as others that, despite including out-of-hospital HPs, contributed no specific data on this subgroup in their results were excluded.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states exclusion of studies that "contributed no specific data on this subgroup" (i.e., outcome results for the subgroup not reported). However, there is no explicit statement distinguishing exclusion of studies because outcomes were not measured versus simply not reported, so the distinction is only partly addressed.

The retrieved methods/results describe individual study groupings (e.g., Health vs Emergency groups in included studies) and present a narrative synthesis, but do not specify review-level groups used in each synthesis nor explicitly link such groups to the comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: High methodological quality was established for the inclusion of studies in the review.
elements.reason: The review provides a rationale for restricting inclusion to studies of high methodological quality via JBI appraisal (explicitly stating high methodological quality was required). However, rationales for other notable restrictions (e.g., language limits, date cutoff) are not explained in the retrieved evidence, so rationale information is incomplete.

elements.quote: To do so, the electronic version of the following databases were consulted in November 2021: Cumulative Index of Nursing and Allied Literature-CINHAL (EBSCOhost, Ipswich, MA, USA), Cochrane Library, Cuiden, Índice Bibliográfico Español en Ciencias de la Salud-IBECS (BVS, Sao Paulo, Brazil), Joanna Briggs Institute-JBI (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), Literatura Latinoamericana y del Caribe en Ciencias de la Salud-LILACS (BVS, Sao Paulo, Brazil), Medline (Pubmed, Bethesda, MD, USA), PyscoDoc (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), PsycINFO (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), Scopus (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA), and Web of Science-WOS (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports that the electronic databases were consulted in November 2021, providing a date when the sources were searched (applied to the listed databases).

elements.quote: the electronic version of the following databases were consulted in November 2021: Cumulative Index of Nursing and Allied Literature-CINHAL (EBSCOhost, Ipswich, MA, USA), Cochrane Library, Cuiden, Índice Bibliográfico Español en Ciencias de la Salud-IBECS (BVS, Sao Paulo, Brazil), Joanna Briggs Institute-JBI (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), Literatura Latinoamericana y del Caribe en Ciencias de la Salud-LILACS (BVS, Sao Paulo, Brazil), Medline (Pubmed, Bethesda, MD, USA), PyscoDoc (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), PsycINFO (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), Scopus (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA), and Web of Science-WOS (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA).
elements.reason: The names of bibliographic databases and their platforms/interfaces are reported (e.g., CINHAL (EBSCOhost), JBI (Ovid), Medline (PubMed), Scopus (Elsevier), WOS (Elsevier)), but no information about available coverage dates (date ranges) for each database is provided.

elements.quote: The study protocol has previously been registered at the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews PROSPERO, supported by the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination of the University of York, under reference CRD-42021259951. ... reviewing webpages, sources of grey literature (ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, and OpenGrey), as well as bibliographic references cited in the selected studies.
elements.reason: Study register and grey literature sources are named (PROSPERO registration referenced; ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global and OpenGrey cited), but no date restrictions or date limits for searches of these registers/repositories are reported.

elements.quote: With the aim of identifying other potentially relevant works that had not previously been recovered, a manual inverse search strategy was proposed, reviewing webpages, sources of grey literature (ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, and OpenGrey), as well as bibliographic references cited in the selected studies.
elements.reason: The authors state they reviewed webpages and other online sources (and later mention use of social networks and specialized web pages in recruitment), but they do not provide URLs or full names/addresses for the specific websites/search engines used.

There is no evidence that organisations or manufacturers were contacted to identify studies; the manuscript only mentions contacting corresponding authors if needed, not organisations or manufacturers.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the type of individual to be contacted (the corresponding author) to obtain missing information.

elements.quote: With the aim of identifying other potentially relevant works that had not previously been recovered, a manual inverse search strategy was proposed, reviewing webpages, sources of grey literature (ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, and OpenGrey), as well as bibliographic references cited in the selected studies.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly state they examined bibliographic references cited in the selected studies (i.e., reference lists), specifying the type of reference lists examined.

Although a manual inverse (citation) search is described and seven new references were found, the manuscript does not report seed reports used for citation searching, the citation index or platform employed for forward/backward searches, nor the date those citation searches were performed.

There is no evidence that specific journals or conference proceedings were consulted as separate sources; therefore reporting source names, dates covered, and search methods for journals/proceedings does not apply based on the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts, excluding records that did not meet the inclusion criteria. ... With regard to the selection process of the studies, from among the 99 articles considered of potential relevance, each evaluator undertook a critical reading of 25, requiring the participation of a third evaluator on 7 occasions. ... The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews, thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the number of reviewers for title/abstract screening (three independent reviewers) and describes that full-text selection/data extraction were completed in pairs, with third-reviewer involvement on specific occasions.

elements.quote: Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts... The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs ... independently with blind reviews...
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that initial screening was performed by three independent reviewers and that later stages were completed independently in pairs with blind reviews.

elements.quote: The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs ... resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.). ... (from among the 99 articles ... requiring the participation of a third evaluator on 7 occasions).
elements.reason: The manuscript describes resolving disagreements by consensus and, if unresolved, involving a named third evaluator; it also reports occasions when a third reviewer was required.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications. ... At no time was it necessary to contact the authors of the studies.
elements.reason: The authors describe the planned process to obtain/confirm information from study investigators (contacting corresponding authors) and report that it was not required in practice.
No information is provided about methods used to translate abstracts or full articles for eligibility assessment.

elements.quote: All the works that had initially been identified in each of the databases consulted were included in Mendeley ® Reference Manager (Elsevier, New York, US), with the objective of removing duplicates. ... In those databases that have an automatic alert system, these will be configured to provide a feed of new appointments every two weeks.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes use of Mendeley to remove duplicates and use of automatic alert systems as part of the ongoing selection/update process, indicating integration of automation tools.
No mention of externally derived classifiers, their versions/references, role, or records removed before screening is provided.
No information on internally derived classifiers, their training, validation, or use is reported.
The manuscript does not describe any machine-learning prioritisation tools or stopping/prioritisation rules used in screening.
No description of crowdsourcing platforms or their integration into study selection is provided.
There is no mention of previously screened datasets being used to eliminate records or how such datasets were derived.

elements.quote: One group of reviewers (N.G.S.B., H.O.B., J.J.J.A., and J.F.F.D.) extracted data from the included studies using this form, whereas the second one (A.M.R.M., M.M.O, M.P.M.H., and A.M.S.) verified the extracted data.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly reports two groups of four reviewers: one group performed data extraction and a second group verified the extracted data, providing the number of reviewers involved in data collection per report.

elements.quote: The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews, thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: The text states that data-extraction was completed in pairs 'independently with blind reviews', directly reporting that multiple data collectors worked independently.

elements.quote: thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for resolving disagreements: first by consensus, and if unresolved, by consulting a third evaluator.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: The authors describe planning to contact study corresponding authors to obtain or confirm missing or unclear data; the Results also note that contacting authors was not required in practice.
No information is provided about use, training, or validation of any automation tools for data collection in the retrieved evidence.
Although eligible publication languages are listed, the manuscript does not report methods used to translate articles for data collection.
The retrieved evidence does not specify any software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: A standardized data-extraction form was designed in accordance with the JBI [50] recommendations with the purpose of guaranteeing the homogeneity of researchers in the collection of the information as well as facilitating its subsequent analysis and comparison.
elements.reason: While the authors describe using a standardized extraction form and paired independent extraction with verification (which addresses consistency and discrepancies), they do not explicitly provide decision rules for choosing among multiple reports or resolving conflicting data across multiple reports of the same study.

elements.quote: The levels of stress, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy of the out-of-hospital HPs during the COVID-19 pandemic were some of the results analyzed in the selected studies.
elements.reason: The outcome domains sought are explicitly listed (stress, anxiety, depression, self-efficacy) and measurement instruments for each are described, but the manuscript does not provide formal definitions of these outcome domains.

elements.quote: The period analyzed in most studies included in this review was the first phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, between the months of March and July 2020, which coincided with an important increase in the global case rate ...
elements.reason: The time frame of measurement for included studies is specified (mostly March–July 2020), and the text also notes variability in specific instrument time-references (e.g. time of questionnaire completion, week immediately before).

The manuscript does not state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (e.g. all measures, time points, analyses) were sought; no explicit statement about attempting to collect all compatible results is provided in the retrieved evidence.
Because the authors do not state that they limited which compatible results were sought, there is likewise no description of any process used to select among multiple eligible results.
No reporting of changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance (with rationales) is present in the provided evidence.
No reporting of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains (with rationales) is present in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?
elements.reason: While the review's objective and outcome domains (mental health outcomes) are clear, the authors do not report which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions nor provide a rationale for prioritisation in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Based on the research question formulated as well as the inclusion and exclusion criteria considered, the following data were specifically extracted from each selected article: title and principal author, country and year of publication, objective, type of study, place and period undertaken, size and characteristics of the sample, definition of variables under analysis and instruments used, principal results obtained, conclusions of the study and scientific-technical quality.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the other variables/data items that were sought and extracted from each study.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes a plan to resolve missing or unclear information (contacting authors) but does not state any explicit assumptions made about missing or unclear study information.

elements.quote: A standardized data-extraction form was designed in accordance with the JBI [50] recommendations with the purpose of guaranteeing the homogeneity of researchers in the collection of the information as well as facilitating its subsequent analysis and comparison.
elements.reason: The authors cite and describe using a JBI-based standardized data-extraction form (tool) to determine/collect data items.

elements.quote: Critical Appraisal Tools from JBI of the University of Adelaide (Australia) [47], considered adequate for the design of the study [48,49], were used to evaluate the scientifictechnical quality of the selected articles as well as to determine the extent to which the risk of bias was reduced or eliminated in their design, performance, and/or analysis.
elements.reason: The risk-of-bias tool (JBI Critical Appraisal Tools) is explicitly named, but no version number or specific version identifier is reported.

elements.quote: Table 3. Critical appraisal of cross-sectional studies. Y: yes; N: no; U: unclear. Q1: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined? Q2: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail? Q3: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way? Q4: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition? Q5: Were confounding factors identified? Q6: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated? Q7: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way? Q8: Was appropriate statistical analysis used? Table 4. Critical appraisal of qualitative studies. Y: yes; N: no; U: unclear. Q1: Is there congruity between the stated philosophical perspective and the research methodology? Q2: Is there congruity between the research methodology and the research question or objectives? Q3: Is there congruity between the research methodology and the methods used to collect data? Q4: Is there congruity between the research methodology and the representation and analysis of data? Q5: Is there congruity between the research methodology and the interpretation of results? Q6: Is there a statement locating the researcher culturally or theoretically? Q7: Is the influence of the researcher on the research, and vice-versa, addressed? Q8: Are participants and their voices adequately represented? Q9: Is the research ethical according to current criteria or for recent studies, and is there evidence of ethical approval by an appropriate body? Q10: Do the conclusions drawn in the research report flow from the analysis or interpretation of the data?
elements.reason: The specific domains/items (Q1–Q8 for cross-sectional studies and Q1–Q10 for qualitative studies) assessed by the JBI tools are listed and defined.

elements.quote: Each individual study was classified as having a low-, moderate-, or high-risk level of bias based on the number of items answered with 'yes'. For qualitative studies (10 items), the methodological quality was considered low, moderate, or high if three or less, four to seven, or more than eight criteria were met, respectively [48]. For cross-sectional studies (8 items), the methodological quality was considered low, moderate, or high if two or less, moderate if three to five, and high if six to eight criteria were met, respectively [49].
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgement (low/moderate/high) was made and explicit numeric rules/thresholds for deriving those judgements from the number of 'yes' responses are provided for both qualitative and cross-sectional tools.
No information or description is provided about adapting the JBI tools or making other modifications to an existing risk-of-bias tool.
There is no indication that a newly developed risk-of-bias tool was created or used; the report specifies use of established JBI Critical Appraisal Tools, so a new tool does not apply.

elements.quote: Prior to its use, a trial test was carried out in which the reviewers (N.G.S.B., H.O.B., J.J.J.A., A.M.R.M., M.M.O., J.J.F.D., M.P.M.H., and A.M.S.) had to evaluate three articles, subsequently analyzing the degree of concordance between their evaluations. ... One group of reviewers (N.G.S.B., H.O.B., J.J.J.A., and J.F.F.D.) extracted data from the included studies using this form, whereas the second one (A.M.R.M., M.M.O, M.P.M.H., and A.M.S.) verified the extracted data. Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts... The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews, thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: The number and identities of reviewers are reported, screening and assessments were done independently/in pairs with blind review, and a procedure for resolving disagreements (consensus then third reviewer) is described.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications. ... At no time was it necessary to contact the authors of the studies.
elements.reason: The planned process to obtain or confirm information from study investigators (contacting corresponding authors for clarifications) is described, and the results (not needed) are reported.

elements.quote: In this living systematic review, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs has been evaluated. Their results have revealed the existence of different factors that have been associated with a greater or lesser risk of developing symptoms of stress, anxiety, and depression as well as the identification of various coping strategies used by HPs to adapt to the situations arising from the COVID-19 pandemic. Being a woman was associated with higher levels of perceived anxiety and stress, similar results to those obtained by health workers from other areas [16,71-76].
elements.reason: The Discussion places the review findings in the context of other evidence by explicitly comparing results (e.g., gender differences in anxiety/stress) to findings from studies of health workers in other areas and cites supporting references, demonstrating interpretation relative to existing literature.

elements.quote: The findings of this review must be considered in the context of their own strengths and limitations. Its principal strength might be that no other systematic review has, to date, specifically analyzed the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs. As more evident limitations of this study, arising from its own methodological approach, publication bias and selection bias in the choice of the databases consulted may be mentioned, as well as the search strategy that was used and the exclusion of works published in languages other than those previously stated. An attempt was made to minimize these sorts of bias through the participation of at least 2 researchers in the search and selection process in 11 of the most relevant databases in the field of health sciences and psychology as well as the use of a somewhat unrestrictive search strategy. The methodological quality of studies selected was optimal, except in some cases, with reference to participation rates and sample representativeness, justified by the epidemiological context and the generalized difficulties imposed as a consequence of the outbreak on both HPs and the researchers themselves. The high heterogeneity observed in the socio-demographic characteristics of the sample of participants, in the field under development and in the measurement scales and instruments that were in use, complicated the comparison and any extrapolation of the results as well as the analysis of biases. Moreover, along with the relative scarcity of published studies, it must be added that a joint and not always a comparative approach was used for data analysis in most of them, without discriminating between out-of-hospital professionals and other health personnel. This living systematic review was conducted at a relatively early stage of the COVID19 pandemic. In the coming months and years, many primary studies and systematic reviews will continue to be published, so the future updating of this review and the completion of a systematic review of reviews could be a new source of evidence on the topic.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly identifies multiple limitations of the included evidence (publication and selection bias, language exclusion, variable methodological quality, high heterogeneity, scarcity of studies, non-comparative analyses, early stage of pandemic), thus discussing limitations of the evidence included in the review.
